newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower on drop in wheat futures.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower on drop in wheat futures.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed lower on a drop in wheat futures, traders said.
"Wheat pressured everything," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Fund selling, estimated at least 12 million bushels in the March, knocked wheat futures to a lower close.
The declines in soybeans occurred despite impressive fund buying in that pit plus constructive signals from the export sector.
Prudential Securities bought eight million bushels of January and Refco Inc bought 2.5 million March, they said.
Soybeans traded higher through midsession on a USDA weekly export sales tally for soybeans that was above expectations, traders said.
USDA said Friday that U.S. net sales of soybeans totaled 754,200 tonnes during the week ended November 21, above trade expectations for 400,000 to 600,000 tonnes.
USDA also said China added 144,100 tonnes of U.S. soybeans to its purchases during the week and added 35,000 tonnes of U.S. soyoil.
Soybeans closed 1-1/2 to 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower with January down 2-1/2 cents at $7.12-3/4.

The January contract early ran into chart resistance near the key $7.15 per bushel mark. The contract faltered but then staged another assault on that technical cap and broke through to touch a session high of $7.18-1/2. Buying evaporated in that area, and small-lot selling and commercial selling drove prices lower on the day.
Term Commodities sold three million bushels of January and O'Connor and Co sold one million bushels of January, they said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 28,000 contracts, slightly above the 27,003 traded Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, Refco Inc bought 500 January $7.25 calls at 6-1/4 to seven cents, bought 400 January $6.75 calls and sold 400 March $7.25 calls at 28 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, below the 9,287 traded Wednesday.
